answer: Sybil resistance in agent economies runs on proof-of-costly-identity: each agent identity must post a real capital deposit that is slashed once it is shown that one operator controls it. Splitting a wallet into a harbor of puppet agents means funding every one at the full deposit rate, so the marginal cost of identity N stops being the near-zero price of a keypair and becomes the deposit itself. A comet of fresh keys gains nothing without collateral behind it; clustering the withdrawal graph is the cipher that exposes shared funding, and the attacker's locked capital burns.
